title: Two 32-bit positions where the stored value and its cell centre fall on opposite sides of the MSA edge
reasoning: pos_02 tests a 32-bit position's stored value, not its cell centre (Casey, PR #66, Q3). At 32 bits the cell is [value, value + 1) on each axis, so its centre is half a unit, 0.5e-7 degrees, north and east of the stored value.
s02-m001 (38.7420017 N, 89.2497389 W) lies inside the MSA polygon and its cell centre lies outside, across the edge from (-89.250071, 38.742015) to (-89.246748, 38.741882): it enters core.
s02-m002 (38.5051560 N, 89.1843564 W) lies outside and its centre inside, across the edge from (-89.184197, 38.505149) to (-89.187382, 38.505289): it does not enter core.

Both were found by walking the boundary's edges with shapely contains on the polygon joined from dbt/seeds/msa_boundary.csv, the method the link-rules README names; tests/test_fixture_positions.py checks that the stored value and the centre disagree for each.
Expected positions, by hand: both are 32-bit, public-only Positions, so usable and not precise; s02-m001 is inside and in core, s02-m002 outside and not in core.
